data.content_ref: inline:The target's answer to 'what single mechanism best explains why that night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others' conflates two distinct physical drivers — radiative geometry (sky view factor / street canyon blocking of longwave cooling) and city size/built density — without establishing which is the single dominant cross-city modulator. By framing the mechanism as 'larger, denser street canyons trap longwave radiation and block sky view' while simultaneously claiming the gap 'scales with city size and built density,' it leaves ambiguous whether the cross-city variation is controlled by geometric radiation trapping or by aggregate urban scale, so it fails to identify a single mechanism as required.
